title: Cohort-aware Optimization - wireframes & backlog
body:
Purpose / one-liner:
This doc captures an experiment-level UX concept: surface recommendations (batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles) scoped by request cohort, with quick-apply controls and safety rails for canaries/rollouts. Goal is to reduce unit cost while keeping per-cohort latency/regression guardrails obvious to engineers.

Context / why cohort-aware?
- Current Optimize work surfaces global suggestions. Many customers have heterogenous traffic (interactive chat vs bulk embeddings) where one-size-fits-all leads to either higher latency or missed cost savings.
- Idea: group requests into cohorts (route, model+seq-range, client id, traffic pattern) and show tailored recommendations per cohort.
- Cohort concept must map to existing routing & telemetry (route id + model variant + token distribution histogram).

High-level UX goals
- Make recommended tradeoffs explicit: expected p50/p95 latency impact, estimated token cost delta, risk score (regression probability).
- Fast experiments: one-click canary to subset of traffic with auto-revert on regression.
- Manual overrides for safety: preview tokens, dry-run telemetry.
- Persist knowledge in a recommendation history for audits.

Wireframe notes (desktop layout)
- Left rail: Cohort selector
  - Search + filters (route, model, tag, example queries)
  - Each cohort shows small sparkline for RPS and token length distribution badge
  - Action icons: view telemetry, open cohort in Trace UI, create test prompt set
- Main canvas: Suggestions feed (stacked cards)
  - Card header: cohort name, baseline SLOs, current cost/kg tokens, last eval time
  - Suggestion types: Batching preset, Cache (prefix/KV) profile, Quantization preset (int8/4/llm-int8), Combined bundle
  - Each card body: 3-line rationale, bullets: expected delta (cost -12%), latency +1ms p50, p95 +7ms, quality delta estimate (human-eval CI), confidence score
  - Controls: Preview (simulated tokens and cost), Run dry-run (traffic shadowing), Apply (dropdown: rollout %, canary target), Save as preset, Comment
- Right rail: Impact simulator + telemetry preview
  - Small chart: estimated cost vs latency curve for selected suggestion at different rollout percents (0-100%)
  - Quick metrics: token-savings/week, projected $/month, regression risk flag
  - Recent experiment logs: last 7 days (dry-run mismatches, latency skew)

Interaction flows
1) Quick-apply canary (happy path)
  - User selects cohort -> suggestion card -> Apply -> choose 10% -> pick traffic slice (random or top-clients) -> confirm.
  - System: create rollout config, instrument tracing, schedule auto-check at 1h/6h.
  - On regression: automatic rollback and notification to owners.
2) Dry-run + QA
  - User requests dry-run; backend shadows requests to variant and runs offline eval against promptset. UI shows mismatch rate and example diffed outputs with redlines.
3) Bundle & promote
  - Team composes multiple suggestions into a bundle (batch+cache+quant) for a safety-labeled rollout. Bundles can be versioned and promoted across environments.

Backlog & grooming items (priority order)
- OPT-6000 (1w): Cohort selector prototype + cohort metadata API integration. Acceptance: can list cohorts + simple sparkline.
- OPT-6001 (2w): Suggestion card component + simulated cost/latency fields. Acceptance: components render with sample data; Apply button disabled.
- OPT-6002 (3w): Apply flow (create rollout config) + basic rollout page stub. Acceptance: create API call, rollout visible in Rollouts tab.
- OPT-6003 (2w): Dry-run shadowing instrumentation + mismatch view (backend + UI). Acceptance: show mismatches for test cohort.
- OPT-6004 (2w): Impact simulator chart (client-side mock then real metrics).
- OPT-6005 (1w): Audit log / history for suggestions.
- OPT-6006 (1w): Accessibility pass for cards + keyboard flows.
- OPT-6007 (1w): Preset save/restore and export.
- OPT-6008 (2w): Canary auto-rollback rules + notification plumbing.
- OPT-6009 (3w): Security review for private deployment integrations (KMS/keys used when applying quant profiles).
Estimates are rough; scope for parallelization.

Open questions / trade-offs
- How to compute "confidence" number? (Offline eval + calibration from historical rollouts). Need ML signals from applied experiments (OPT-analytics).
- Cohort cardinality: how many cohorts should be suggested by default? (Top N by RPS or by cost impact potential).
- Do we allow ML teams to author custom cohort selectors (regex on routes) vs system-generated?
- Quantization safety: do we block certain model architectures or sequence lengths? Need runtime compatibility checks.

Telemetry & success metrics
- Uptake: % of customers who use cohort suggestions within 60 days of feature release.
- Safety: rollback rate within first 24 hours for canaries. Target <5%.
- Economics: median per-customer token cost reduction for cohorts that applied suggestions. Target 8–15% for non-chat workloads.
- Quality: % of canaries with output-mismatch rate > threshold (needs to be low).

Prototype visuals (textual sketch)
- [COHORT LIST] | [Suggestion card 1] [Suggestion card 2] [Suggestion card N] | [Simulator panel]
- Example card excerpt:
  - Title: embeddings-bulk-8k (route: /v1/embeddings, model: text-embed-030)
  - Suggestion: batching: group size 64 -> cost -18%, latency p50 +5ms, p95 +12ms
  - Apply: [Dry-run] [Preview] [Apply -> canary 10%]

Acceptance criteria for MVP
- Users can select cohort, view at least 2 suggestion types, simulate impact, and create a canary rollout.
- Rollout must include automatic telemetry checks (latency and quality) and a manual rollback button.
- Audit entries for every apply action with owner and timestamp.

Risks / mitigation
- Risk: Over-complex UI increases confusion. Mitigation: default to a single recommended bundle and an "advanced" expand for detailed controls.
- Risk: False confidence numbers. Mitigation: label confidence as heuristic and show underlying signals.

Next steps (short term)
- Design pairing session: Asha + Miguel + Riley to iterate card micro-copy and fallbacks (this week).
- Engineering spike: platform team to expose cohort listing + sample telemetry endpoint (OPT-6000) (blocker for prototypes).
- UX prototype: Figma screens for desktop + small-screen collapse pattern (2 weeks).
- Schedule sync with SRE for canary autoscaling behavior during rollouts.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep bundle names readable (suggest: <cohort>-econ-v1).
- Consider a "safety profile" toggle: strict/moderate/lenient to influence quantization aggressiveness.
- Check with legal on audit retention limits for Private deployments.

References & related docs
- Existing optimize prescriptive flows (see OPTIMIZE-PLAYBOOK in product Drive).
- Rollouts RFC (eng/rls/rollouts-rfc.md).
- Historic rollout telemetry (OPT-analytics/experiments/2024)

Questions for reviewers
- Do we want to start with route-based cohorts only, or include client-id slices for early customers?
- Is simulated cost/latency curve better as a chart or an interactive slider?
- Who should own the initial canary rollback alerts (on-call SRE vs product team)?

-- end --
